extracted.intended_audience: employers, human resources professionals, labor and employment attorneys, wage-hour compliance officers, and regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applying 29 CFR Part 541 to determine whether particular employees qualify for the section 13(a)(1) and 13(a)(17) exemptions (executive, administrative, professional, computer, and outside sales) including salary tests, duties tests, definitions, and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introductory statement (§541.0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains that section 13(a)(1) provides exemptions for bona fide executive, administrative, professional, and outside sales employees; section 13(a)(17) covers certain computer employees; enumerates subparts covering duties, salary requirements, definitions, and miscellaneous provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets scope: these regulations delimit exemptions and are subject to APA; indicates where to find salary tests (Subpart G) and definitions (Subpart H).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms used in regulations (§541.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines key statutory/regulatory terms used in the part, e.g., 'Act' means the Fair Labor Standards Act; 'Administrator' means Administrator of the Wage and Hour Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides baseline definitional authority; use these definitions when applying the tests in the part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Job titles insufficient (§541.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A job title alone does not establish exempt status; determination must be based on salary and duties meeting the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourages reliance on titles — analyze actual duties and pay structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope — blue collar and public safety exclusions (§541.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 13(a)(1) exemptions do not apply to manual laborers or other 'blue collar' workers who perform repetitive physical work or to many public safety and law-enforcement personnel regardless of rank or pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives lists and examples (production-line employees, carpenters, police officers, firefighters, paramedics, inspectors, etc.) and explains why such roles are nonexempt (nature of work, training source, primary duty).

rubrics_metrics.name: Other laws and collective bargaining agreements (§541.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act provides minimum standards that cannot be waived; employers must comply with any higher state/local laws or contractual obligations that provide greater protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employer must not rely on Part 541 to reduce rights under other laws or CBAs; follow higher applicable standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability (§541.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions are separable; if any provision is invalid, construct to give maximum lawful effect to remainder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal interpretive instruction for application if part is partly invalidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive exemption — general rule (§541.100)
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee is bona fide executive if: (1) compensated on a salary basis at or above §541.600 level; (2) primary duty is management of the enterprise or recognized department/subdivision; (3) customarily and regularly directs the work of two or more other employees; and (4) has authority to hire/fire or whose recommendations carry particular weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references definitions (§541.602, §541.606, §541.700, §541.701); all elements must be evaluated together on the facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business owner exemption (§541.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee who owns at least a bona fide 20% equity interest and is actively engaged in management qualifies as executive; Subpart G salary requirements do not apply to such owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership threshold and active engagement are the key criteria; salary test waived for qualifying owners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management activities (§541.102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists activities that 'management' generally includes: interviewing, selecting, training, setting pay/hours, directing work, maintaining records for supervision, appraising productivity, handling grievances, disciplining, planning work, apportioning work, choosing materials/equipment, controlling flow/distribution, safety, budgeting, and monitoring legal compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides nonexclusive examples to help determine whether an employee's duties are managerial in nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department or subdivision (§541.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'customarily recognized department or subdivision' as a unit with permanent status and continuing function; may have subdivisions; need not be physically within employer's establishment; continuity of personnel not essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiates between a temporary collection of employees and a recognized unit; explains applicability across multiple establishments and mobile units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directing two or more other employees (§541.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify as an exempt executive, the employee must customarily and regularly direct the work of two or more other employees (two full-time employees or equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains equivalence (e.g., one full-time + two half-time = two full-time); supervisors who only act in manager's absence do not qualify; hours cannot be double-counted for multiple executives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particular weight of recommendations (§541.105)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors for whether an employee's hiring/firing/advancement recommendations are given 'particular weight' include whether it's part of the job, frequency of recommendations, and frequency of reliance; generally pertains to employees the executive customarily directs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that recommendations can have particular weight even if ultimate decision rests with higher management; occasional suggestions do not suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent duties (§541.106)
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee performing both exempt and nonexempt work may still qualify as exempt if §541.100 requirements are met; determination is case-by-case using factors in §541.700. Exempt executives usually control when to perform nonexempt duties and remain responsible while doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives examples (assistant manager can serve customers while supervising) and contrasts relief supervisors/working supervisors whose primary duty is production work and therefore are nonexempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative exemption — general rule (§541.200)
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee is bona fide administrative if: (1) compensated on salary or fee basis at or above §541.600; (2) primary duty is office or nonmanual work directly related to management or general business operations of employer or employer's customers; and (3) primary duty includes exercise of discretion and independent judgment with respect to matters of significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references §541.602, §541.605, §541.606, and §541.700; all elements must be analyzed together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directly related to management or general business operations (§541.201)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains that 'directly related' refers to work assisting with running or servicing the business (not production-line or selling work); includes functional areas like tax, finance, accounting, budgeting, auditing, insurance, quality control, purchasing, procurement, advertising, marketing, research, safety, HR, benefits, labor relations, PR, government relations, IT/network/database administration, legal/compliance, and similar activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees advising or consulting to customers may qualify; some work may be covered by multiple exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion and independent judgment (§541.202)
rubrics_metrics.description: To meet the administrative exemption, the employee's primary duty must include discretion and independent judgment on matters of significance — involving evaluation of possible courses of conduct and acting after consideration; 'matters of significance' refers to importance/consequence of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists factors to consider (authority to formulate/implement policies, major assignments, effect on business operations, financial commitment authority, ability to waive policies, authority to bind/negotiation, providing expert advice, planning objectives, investigating/resolving significant matters, representing company). Clarifies that review by higher-ups does not preclude exemption; excludes mere application of well-established techniques, clerical work, routine data tabulation; gives examples and counterexamples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative exemption examples (§541.203)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides concrete examples of roles that generally meet or do not meet the administrative duties test: insurance claims adjusters, many financial services roles (excluding primary sales roles), team leaders on major projects, executive assistants with delegated authority, HR managers and management consultants generally meet; personnel clerks, ordinary inspectors, graders, and employees who apply established standards typically do not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains nuance (e.g., when interviewing/screening by HR is exempt vs. nonexempt) and provides industry-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational establishment administrative functions (§541.204)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative exemption includes employees in educational establishments if compensated at §541.600 or at least teacher entrance salary and primary duty is administrative functions directly related to academic instruction or training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'educational establishment' broadly (elementary, secondary, higher ed, special schools); clarifies academic administrative functions vs. general business administration and gives examples (superintendents, principals, department heads, academic counselors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional exemption — general rule (§541.300)
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee is bona fide professional if compensated on a salary or fee basis at or above §541.600 and primary duty is work requiring advanced knowledge (learned professional) or invention/creativity (creative professional) or falls within other professional categories (teachers, practice of law/medicine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references subsections (§541.301–§541.304) for detailed standards and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learned professionals (§541.301)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learned professional primary duty is the performance of work requiring advanced knowledge in a field of science or learning customarily acquired by a prolonged course of specialized intellectual instruction (e.g., doctors, lawyers, architects, engineers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes advanced academic instruction as customary path; distinguishes from occupations where skill is acquired by apprenticeship/on-the-job training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative professionals (§541.302)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative professional exemption covers employees whose primary duty requires invention, imagination, originality, or talent in recognized artistic or creative fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on the nature of creative work rather than formal academic credentials; gives examples in Part 541 text (e.g., creative artists).

rubrics_metrics.name: Teachers (§541.303)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers in elementary and secondary schools and academic personnel in educational institutions may qualify as professional employees under specified conditions; references definitions of educational establishments and duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §541.204 and other subsections for interaction with administrative exemptions and salary tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice of law or medicine (§541.304)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies that practice of law or medicine is encompassed by the professional exemption where duties meet professional criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These professions are paradigmatic learned professional occupations; salary and duties tests still apply as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer employee exemption — general rule (§541.400)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 13(a)(17) exemption covers certain computer systems analysts, programmers, software engineers, and other similarly skilled computer employees if paid at required rates/fees and their primary duties consist of specified computer-related tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references subsections for manufacturing/repair exceptions and interaction with executive/administrative exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer manufacture and repair (§541.401)
rubrics_metrics.description: Makes clear that employees in computer manufacture and repair and related occupations may be excluded from the computer employee exemption depending on duties; distinguishes manufacturing/repair work from the exempt computer duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on the nature of duties performed (manufacturing/repair vs. systems analysis/programming).

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive and administrative computer employees (§541.402)
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses treatment of computer employees who perform executive or administrative duties and how those exemptions interact with the computer employee exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for categorizing computer professionals whose primary duties are managerial or administrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outside sales exemption — general rule (§541.500)
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee is an exempt outside salesperson if the employee's primary duty is making sales or obtaining orders/contracts and the employee is customarily and regularly engaged away from the employer's place of business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references definitions (§541.501–§541.504) for details about what constitutes 'making sales', 'away from employer's place of business', and permissible promotional tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making sales or obtaining orders (§541.501)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines what constitutes making sales: obtaining orders or contracts for services or for the use of facilities; includes examples of sales activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that solicitation of orders and actual sales both count; distinguishes from promotional activities that are not sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Away from employer's place of business (§541.502)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires outside sales employees to be customarily and regularly away from the employer's place of business when engaged in sales activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides criteria to determine what constitutes 'away' and examples for field sales vs. inside sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion work (§541.503)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes promotional activities and when such activities count toward the outside sales exemption versus when they are nonexempt work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes incidental promotion from primary sales duties; guidance on combination roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drivers who sell (§541.504)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers drivers who sell (e.g., route salespersons) and conditions under which drivers qualify as outside sales employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains application to delivery/route sales with sales function included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount of salary required (§541.600)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes salary level(s) required for exempt status (salary threshold for salary-basis test) and methodology for determining amounts (cross-references updates and highly compensated thresholds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies required weekly salary amounts, application to salary and fee basis, and references update procedures (§541.607).

rubrics_metrics.name: Highly compensated employees (§541.601)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines exemption for certain highly compensated employees who meet a total annual compensation threshold and perform at least one of the exempt duties; sets compensation amount and special rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies total annual compensation level (§541.601(a)), duties test relaxation, and update mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salary basis test (§541.602)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'salary basis' and explains when an employee is considered paid on a salary basis, including permissible deductions and required assurances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes what pay arrangements satisfy or violate salary-basis status; see §541.603 for improper deductions consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of improper deductions from salary (§541.603)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains that improper deductions may invalidate the salary-basis test and result in loss of exempt status; outlines employer obligations and corrective measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides examples of improper deductions and procedures for restoring salary-basis status if deductions were made in violation of the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum guarantee plus extras (§541.604)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes permissible salary arrangements involving a guaranteed minimum plus extras (e.g., commissions, bonuses) and how they affect exempt status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains calculation and interaction with salary thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee basis (§541.605)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines fee basis payment arrangements and how they operate for certain professionals in satisfying compensation tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives criteria for when fee basis counts toward exemption and how to evaluate fee-based compensation structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board, lodging or other facilities (§541.606)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines compensation that may be provided as board, lodging, or other facilities and how such in-kind benefits are treated relative to salary tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies valuation and rules for including such benefits in compensation calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular updates to salary/compensation amounts (§541.607)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes procedures and timing for periodic updates to earnings thresholds (salary and highly compensated levels) using current earnings data and notice procedures, including delay mechanics tied to potential rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies update frequency, data sources (CPS MORG), 150-day notice requirement, publication on WHD website, and process for delaying updates if rulemaking is underway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary duty definition (§541.700)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'primary duty' as the principal, main, major or most important duty performed; determination is based on all facts with emphasis on character of the job as a whole; factors include relative importance of exempt duties, amount of time spent, relative freedom from supervision, and salary relationship to nonexempt wages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that time (over 50%) is a useful guide but not sole test; gives examples (assistant managers) showing nuance where more than 50% nonexempt time may still support exempt status if other factors favor exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customarily and regularly (§541.701)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'customarily and regularly' as a frequency greater than occasional but possibly less than constant; includes work normally and recurrently performed every workweek and excludes isolated or one-time tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in tests requiring regular performance of duties (e.g., directing two or more employees, away-from-office sales).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exempt and nonexempt work (§541.702)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines 'exempt work' as the work described in the exemptions (§§541.100, 541.101, 541.200, 541.300, 541.301, 541.302, 541.303, 541.304, 541.400, 541.500) and activities directly and closely related to such work; all other work is nonexempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies interplay: work directly and closely related to exempt duties is also treated as exempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directly and closely related (§541.703)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains that work directly and closely related to exempt duties includes tasks that contribute to or facilitate exempt work (physical or menial tasks arising from exempt duties), e.g., recordkeeping, monitoring machinery, note-taking, opening mail to make decisions, using photocopier for exempt tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides ten illustrative examples that show what is/ is not directly and closely related (keeping subordinate records, distribution of materials, spot-checking subordinates, machine setup depending on industry, sales-floor observations, consultant note-taking tied to recommendations, credit manager tasks, traffic manager responsibilities, chemist's menial lab tasks, teacher chaperoning driving duties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of manuals (§541.704)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of manuals/guidelines for highly technical/complex matters does not preclude exemption; but employees who simply apply well-established techniques/procedures within closely prescribed limits are not exercising discretion and independent judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes reference-use in addressing novel circumstances (still exempt) vs. rote application of instructions (nonexempt).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainees (§541.705)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemptions do not apply to employees training for employment in exempt capacities who are not actually performing the duties of those exempt roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training status precludes exemption until duties meet the exempt criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergencies (§541.706)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exempt employees do not lose exemption by performing nonexempt work during emergencies that threaten safety, cessation of operations or serious property damage; 'emergency' is rare and not occurrences reasonably foreseeable or controllable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives examples distinguishing exempt emergency work (mine superintendent digging out trapped workers) from routine assistance during heavy workload (not emergency) and guidance about replacing absent employees depending on circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occasional tasks (§541.707)
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasional, infrequently recurring tasks that cannot practicably be performed by nonexempt employees but are necessary for exempt employees to carry out exempt responsibilities are considered exempt work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors: whether subordinates perform same work, practicability of delegation, frequency performed by exempt employee, and industry practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination exemptions (§541.708)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees performing a combination of exempt duties (executive, administrative, professional, outside sales, computer) may qualify if primary duty involves combination and meets requirements; exempt work under one section does not defeat another exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that mixed duties are evaluated in aggregate to determine whether primary duty supports exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion picture producing industry exception (§541.709)
rubrics_metrics.description: In motion picture producing industry, the salary-basis requirement does not apply if base rate is at least specified weekly amount; special rules permit proportional weekly pay or daily rates in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies examples where daily rates or proportionate weekly pay satisfy exemption for this industry; cross-references Subparts B–D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employees of public agencies (§541.710)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public agency employees who meet salary-basis requirements shall not be disqualified from exemptions merely because they are paid under pay systems established by statute/ordinance/regulation that include accrual/use of leave or furlough deductions, with specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains permitted pay reductions and furlough treatment for public agency employees so long as requirements of §541.602 are otherwise met.
